priceNote: Ontario-stamped shelf/online prices observed Aug–Sep 2026 across Toronto retailers, before 13% HST. Prices vary by flavour and store.

products.name: STLTH x Geek Bar 80K
products.flavourExamples: Blue Razz, Banana Burst Ice, Juicy Peach Ice, Mango Peach Ice, Strawberry Kiwi Ice, Blueberry Watermelon Ice, Coconut Ice, Rich Tobacco
pros: 30 mL from Canada's most-trusted vape brand
Pulse mode for a stronger hit on demand
Clear screen — no guessing
Stocked by virtually every Toronto shop
Manufacturer honours DOA replacements
cons: 820 mAh battery is smaller than 1000 mAh rivals — charge every ~2 days
All-iced flavour lineup
Mid-to-high price
products.verdict: The consensus pick across every source we checked. STLTH's Toronto-based QA plus Geek Bar's hardware make this the safest 30 mL buy in the city. If you only read one line: buy this.

products.name: STLTH Titan Max 50K
products.puffsNote: Same 30 mL as the 80K devices — rated at higher output
products.flavourExamples: Honeydew Ice (fan favourite), Banana Ice, Blue Razz Ice, Mango Ice, Strawberry Ice, Watermelon Ice, Tobacco
products.award: Best value from a trusted brand
pros: Identical 30 mL to the 80K class, frequently $5–10 cheaper
1000 mAh — fewer charges
Quad mesh = dense, warm flavour
Nearly two years on the market; strong reliability record
cons: '50K' label makes buyers think it's smaller (it isn't)
No Eco mode — uses liquid faster than Eco-rated rivals
Bulky
products.verdict: The market's best-kept secret. The '50K' number makes it look inferior to '80K' devices, but it holds exactly the same 30 mL and often costs less. If you'd run Boost mode anyway, this is the smarter STLTH.

products.name: Flavour Beast Alpha 80K
products.coil: Physical coil switching: 1.0Ω single mesh (L1–2) / 0.5Ω dual mesh (L3–4)
products.flavourExamples: Extreme Mint Iced, Bomb Blue Razz, Meta Melon Citrus Iced, Jumpin' Juicy Peach, Supreme Strawberry Kiwi, Fruity G candy series
pros: Only disposable that physically switches coils
Widest wattage range (10–23 W)
Flavour Beast recipes are the boldest in Canada
Metal side panel — premium feel
cons: Most expensive device in Toronto
850 mAh is small for 23 W use
Very sweet profiles (likely sucralose)
Bulkiest of the 30 mL class
products.verdict: If flavour intensity and control matter more than $5, this is the one. Run Level 1–2 all day and Level 4 when you want a show. Budget for it.

products.name: Rocky Vapor Oxbar G100K
products.flavourExamples: Blueberry Raspberry, Cherry Watermelon, Fresh Mint, Grape Ice, M.D.W. (lemon-lime), Peach Berry, Raspberry Lemon, Watermelon Ice
pros: 1000 mAh + triple mode for ~$42
'Adapter' middle mode is genuinely useful
Physical airflow dial
Less sugary profiles than Flavour Beast
cons: '100K' is marketing — same 30 mL as the 80K devices
Slow standard-rate charging
Newer to Toronto shelves; fewer long-term reports
products.verdict: Best hardware per dollar among all-in-one disposables. Ignore the 100K number; buy it because it's a 1000 mAh, three-mode, 30 mL device for $42.

products.name: Vice Box 2 70K
products.flavourExamples: Rage Ice, Blue Razz Burst, Frosty Green Apple, Mango Tango Ice, Strawberry Kiwi Ice, Arctic Blue Lemon, Lush Ice
pros: Lowest $/mL of any 30 mL disposable in Toronto
900 mAh battery
Adjustable airflow + screen at a budget price
cons: Single coil — flavour thins toward the end
No power modes
Multiple user reports of leaks/duds over the years
products.verdict: The price leader, and fine if you get a good unit. Test-fire it in store. For $3–4 more, the Oxbar G100K or Titan Max is a clear upgrade.

products.name: Elf Bar BC Pro 80K
products.flavourExamples: Strawberry Kiwi Ice (#1 seller), Blue Razz Ice, Blueberry Sour Raspberry, Miami Mint, Kiwi Guava Ice, Double Mango
pros: Only device where you can SEE the remaining liquid
Cheapest entry into the big class ($32–39 typical)
Elf Bar coils are consistently smooth
Compact for its capacity
cons: 25 mL, not 30 — check the $/mL
No screen, no modes, fixed airflow
Battery capacity undisclosed
Huge price spread by flavour and store
products.verdict: A pragmatic pick: the transparent tank ends the 'is it empty or is my battery dead?' guessing game. Shop around — the same device ranges from $32 to $44 across Toronto.

products.name: STLTH 60K
products.flavourExamples: Blue Razz, Mango, Peach Ice, Watermelon Ice, Mint, Tobacco
pros: Three modes + 1000 mAh
Smaller than Titan Max
STLTH quality control
Retailers report the highest repurchase rate
cons: 25 mL for near-80K pricing
Overshadowed by the Geek Bar collab
products.verdict: The 'boring but reliable' STLTH. Good if you want modes and a slightly smaller body than Titan Max — but compare the price against the 80K.
